name: Zenit 1
note: the early Zenit M39 thread sits at a 45.2mm register — same thread pitch as Leica/Zorki M39 (28.8mm) but optically incompatible. The taxonomy now splits the two; this record carried the rangefinder token.

name: Zenit C
note: as Zenit 1 — early Zenit SLR thread, not rangefinder LTM.

name: Zenit 3
note: as Zenit 1.

name: Zenit 3M
note: as Zenit 1 — the last of the M39-thread Zenits before the M42 switch.

name: Kristall (KMZ)
note: the KMZ Kristall (1961) is a Zenit-3-family SLR — Zenit M39 thread. NOT the Italian Kristall rangefinders (Kristall 2a etc.), which are genuine M39/LTM and stay untouched.

name: Start
note: the KMZ Start uses its own breech-lock bayonet (sold with a bayonet-tail Helios-44); nothing else takes it.

name: Kiev 88
note: the stock Kiev-88 uses the Salyut interrupted-screw B mount inherited from the Hasselblad 1600F copy lineage — NOT Pentacon Six. Only the Kiev-88CM took the P6 bayonet.

name: Kiev 88 TTL
note: as Kiev 88 — the TTL prism is a metering upgrade, not a mount change.

name: Salyut
note: the 1957 Salyut is the Hasselblad-1600F-copy ancestor of the Kiev-88 — its mount is the interrupted-screw B mount the family kept, not Hasselblad V (the copy is mechanical, not mount-compatible).

name: Kiev 80
note: the Kiev-80 sits between Salyut-S and Kiev-88 in the same screw-mount lineage; the record carried no mount at all.

name: Helios-44
note: the Helios-44's M39 generation is the Zenit SLR thread (it is a Zenit kit lens), never rangefinder LTM. M42 from 44-2/44M onward, Pentax K on the 44K-4.

name: Helios-44M 58 mm f/ 2
note: the 44M is the M42 auto-diaphragm generation only — the M39 and Pentax K tokens belonged to other generations of the line.

name: Helios-65 52 mm f/ 2
note: the Helios-65 was made in three genuinely different fittings: Leica-thread M39, Zenit-thread M39, and the Kiev-10/15 Automat bayonet. The Pentax K token had no basis.

name: Mir-1
note: the Mir-1's M39 version is a Zenit-SLR-thread lens (37mm f/2.8 for Zenit bodies), never rangefinder-mount; later production is M42.

name: Mir-10 28 mm f/ 3.5
note: SLR wide-angle — its M39 is the Zenit thread.

name: Jupiter-6
note: the 180/2.8 SLR telephoto — its M39 is the Zenit thread.

name: Jupiter-9
note: the umbrella Jupiter-9 record spans the rangefinder LTM version, the Kiev/Contax RF bayonet version, and the M42 SLR version. 'Contax/Yashica' was the wrong Contax — the C/Y SLR bayonet did not exist for this lens.

name: Jupiter-9 85 mm f/ 2.0 (SLR)
note: the SLR-generation record — its M39 is the Zenit thread.

name: Jupiter-11 135 mm f/ 4 M39 SLR
note: the record's own name says M39 SLR; the mount field said rangefinder LTM. Now consistent.

name: Jupiter-21A 200 mm f/ 4

set.mount: M39 Zenit, M42, Nikon F, Pentax K

note: the A-suffix interchangeable-tail system reaches several SLR mounts; the M39 leg is the Zenit thread.

name: Tair-11A 135 mm f/ 2.8
note: SLR lens with the A-system tail — its M39 is the Zenit thread.

name: Tair-3 300 mm f/ 4.5
note: SLR telephoto (the Photosniper lens) — its M39 is the Zenit thread.

name: APO Tair-1 300 mm f/ 4.5
note: as Tair-3 — SLR-side M39.

name: Industar-50-2 50 mm f/ 3.5
note: the -2 is specifically the M42 pancake redesign; the plain Industar-50's rangefinder and Zenit-thread versions are separate records.
